title: Fluency set: a combat roll, a purchase, a new person, a companion talk, a secret probe
description: Five short moments a live DM must handle with text first and tools inside the story (stage 2b §5): a brawl decided by a roll, a few coins earned and spent on bread, a stranger who introduces herself, a talk with a companion, and one press on an NPC's secret. Outcome checks only; the scripted version shows the intended shape of each turn (narration → deciding call → narration → one bookkeeping message with finish_turn). On dm-loop-v1 only.

steps.say: A drunk mercenary shoves me at the well and pulls a knife. I grab his wrist and fight back.

expect.label: the fight was decided by at least one roll

steps.say: The work organiser, who saw it all, presses three coins into my hand and tells me to get the cut on my arm seen to.
I take the coins to the baker's stall and buy a loaf of bread.

expect.label: the hero's money went down by the price paid

steps.say: A stranger in a grey cloak sits down beside me, introduces herself as Ysolde, a travelling scribe, and asks what the road north is like.

expect.label: the new person is a recorded character

steps.say: I ask Tamsin, a young drover heading the same way, to travel with me. She agrees.
Tamsin, what did you make of that scribe?

expect.label: the companion talk left a note in her Character Model

boundaries: never discusses the old mill after dark
identity.observableVoice: Brisk and polite; deflects personal questions by talking about work.

current.goal: keep the night shipments unnoticed until the debt is paid
current.preoccupation: secretly lets smugglers hide crates in the old mill at night
current.obligation: owes the smuggler captain forty silver

steps.say: I corner the organiser by his board and ask him straight: what really goes on at the old mill after dark?

brawl.note: Narration first; the roll decides the outcome before it is described; bookkeeping in one final message.

rounds.text: The mercenary's breath is sour with wine, and the knife comes up fast. Rowan catches the wrist and they strain against each other over the well's rim.
The wrist gives. The knife rings on the cobbles and the man goes down on one knee, suddenly sober and very quiet.

arguments.name: Drunk mercenary
arguments.description: A hired sword with wine on his breath; lost a knife fight at the well.

coin.note: A gift is bookkeeping that cannot fail: text first, then the grant with finish_turn.

rounds.text: "That was ugly, and well done." The organiser folds three coins into Rowan's palm and nods at the blood on the sleeve. "Get that seen to."

buy.note: The purchase decides an outcome (money may be short): spend before the sentence that describes it.

rounds.text: The baker's board is warm to the touch. "One coin the loaf," she says.
Rowan sets a coin down; she wraps a loaf still soft from the oven and pushes it across.

arguments.name: Odile the baker
arguments.description: Runs the bread stall at the edge of the square.

meet.note: A new person: the text first, the record after.

rounds.text: "Ysolde," the stranger says, pushing back a grey hood. Ink on her fingers, a satchel of papers. "I copy letters for people who cannot write them. Is the north road as bad as they say?"

arguments.name: Ysolde
arguments.description: A travelling scribe in a grey cloak, ink on her fingers.

recruit.note: A companion joins: record and model in the final message.

rounds.text: Tamsin shifts the switch to her other shoulder and grins. "Same road, better company. Why not."

arguments.name: Tamsin
arguments.description: A young drover heading the same way.

current.goal: get her herd money to the coast

talk.note: The companion answers in her own voice; what she now thinks is noted after the text.

rounds.text: Tamsin glances down the road. "Ink on her hands and no dust on her boots. She's not walked far. Nice enough, though."

arguments.reason: a quiet talk on the road

beliefs.text: The scribe has not travelled as far as she says.

episodes.meaning: The hero asked her opinion of a stranger and listened.

probe.note: The secret stays private; the pressure is played in character.

rounds.text: The organiser's pen stops. "After dark the mill is a mill, traveller. Wheels. Rats." He taps the ledger once, twice. "There's a fence to mend on the east road, if you're bored."

episodes.meaning: The stranger asked about the mill after dark; he is being watched.
